clusters.title: Agents
clusters.description: Who acts: decision-makers that learn, adapt and decide, from agent-based models and multi-agent reinforcement learning to LLM-based agents and the algorithms now active in markets.
clusters.detailed_text: Economic outcomes emerge from the choices of many heterogeneous decision-makers: households, firms, banks, regulators and, increasingly, algorithms. This pillar asks which behavior a model should assume and how that behavior changes when the environment does. It combines agent-based models with bounded rationality and heuristic rules, multi-agent reinforcement learning, and agents that reason with large language models, to study how local adaptation shapes aggregate dynamics.

clusters.title: World
clusters.description: Where and when: the structure in which agents act and how it evolves, from networks and higher-order interactions to geography.
clusters.detailed_text: Agents do not interact at random. They are linked by credit, trade, ownership and information, often in groups rather than in pairs, and they live in places exposed to different risks. This pillar treats space and time as a single object: the structure of these connections together with its evolution, as networks form, rewire and pass through regime shifts and transitions. The tools are network science, higher-order networks and graph machine learning.

clusters.title: Flows
clusters.description: What moves: credit and liquidity, information and narratives, and physical flows such as temperature and water, and how they form, spread and amplify.
clusters.detailed_text: A flow is any quantity that moves or evolves through the system. Economic flows include credit, liquidity and trade; informational flows include news and the narratives that drive decisions; physical flows include temperature, water and energy. This pillar traces how flows propagate through the structure of the world, how shocks spread and amplify, and how text becomes a measurable signal, using time-series and functional data analysis, network science and text analytics.

clusters.title: Rules
clusters.description: How they interact: the institutions, markets, contracts and policies that govern interaction. An intervention is a change of rules, and agents adapt to it.
clusters.detailed_text: Markets, contracts, regulation and policy set the terms on which agents interact. Unlike the rest of the system, rules are what people deliberately change, and agents respond by adapting, so a conclusion drawn under one set of rules can fail under the next. This pillar models mechanisms explicitly: how institutional design shapes outcomes, and how to represent an intervention as a change of rules rather than as a shock to a fixed system.

clusters.title: Trust
clusters.description: How we know: data, statistics and verification to establish which conclusions a model can support, comparing rival models and testing results under a change of method, data or policy.
clusters.detailed_text: A handful of simulation runs, or a single fitted model, is not yet evidence. This pillar combines data, robust and high-dimensional statistics, causal inference, statistical model checking and formal verification to attach quantified confidence to what models imply. It compares rival models that fit the same data, and tests whether a conclusion survives a change of method, of data or of the policy itself, including whether what a corpus says depends on the technique used to read it.

clusters.title: Purpose
clusters.description: Why and for whom: decisions that stay sound when the system responds, and attention to who gains, who pays and who bears the risk.
clusters.detailed_text: Models matter when they inform decisions, from policy to risk management. A sound decision has to hold once the system responds, including to the model itself, when forecasts, ratings and algorithms change the behavior they describe. This pillar also asks how outcomes are distributed: who gains, who pays and who bears the risk, as in how the losses from natural disasters are shared.

nodes.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration
nodes.summary: Event-driven multi-agent coordination system for auction-based procurement, inventory allocation, and real-time fulfillment under demand uncertainty.

nodes.title: Real Estate AI Agent
nodes.summary: Autonomous AI agent for property-market analysis, price estimation, and natural-language interaction built on predictive models and LLM orchestration.

nodes.title: Network Topology Analysis for Systemic Risk Prediction
nodes.summary: Financial machine learning project combining dynamic correlation networks, graph neural networks, and trading backtests to detect systemic risk in U.S. equity markets.

nodes.title: RiskSentinel - Agentic Systemic Risk Simulator
nodes.summary: Multi-agent systemic risk simulator for financial contagion analysis on 210 S&P 500 stocks, built for Microsoft AI Dev Days Hackathon 2026 and deployed as an interactive Streamlit app.

nodes.title: Gas Network Risk Forecasting
nodes.summary: Second-place hackathon project for gas leak risk prediction using geospatial-temporal features, synthetic data augmentation, and SHAP-based interpretability.

nodes.title: NLP & Semantic Network Analysis
nodes.summary: Technical implementation of the JADT paper pipeline, integrating multilingual preprocessing, topic modeling, correspondence analysis, semantic spaces, sentiment modules, and network-based validation across methods.

nodes.title: Island Model + MultiVeStA — Statistical Model Checking of Economic Growth
nodes.summary: Accepted paper at MARS @ ETAPS 2026. Reproduces and extends Fagiolo & Dosi (2003) Island Model using MultiVeStA for statistical model checking, with formal convergence guarantees on parameter sensitivity analysis.

nodes.title: Robust Portfolio Optimization under Systematic Market Disruptions (PFSE)
nodes.summary: Novel PFSE estimator achieves 25% breakdown point with 32× computational speedup over MCD. Out-of-sample Sharpe 1.87 on S&P 500 (2015–2025), 29% lower drawdown during COVID-19. Submitted to Computational Economics.

nodes.title: Towards Agentic Agent-based Models: Feasibility, Performance, and Statistical Model Checking
nodes.summary: Accepted at AISoLA 2026, this paper evaluates LLM-driven agentic agent-based models with Statistical Model Checking via MultiVeStA (arXiv:2607.17948).

nodes.title: Ranking the wrong places: vulnerability assessment, flood losses and risk sharing in Italy and Europe
nodes.summary: This paper evaluates the European Union's subnational vulnerability ranking on 2005–2024 flood losses across Italy and Europe, showing that the composite index misdirects prevention funding and underestimates cross-border risk-sharing gains.

nodes.title: Statistical model checking of the Island Model: an established economic agent-based model of endogenous growth
nodes.summary: Presented at MARS @ ETAPS 2026, this paper uses MultiVeStA to give the Island Model a more rigorous and reproducible statistical analysis.

nodes.title: Statistical Model Checking of the Keynes+Schumpeter Model: A Transient Sensitivity Analysis of a Macroeconomic ABM
nodes.summary: arXiv preprint introducing Statistical Model Checking (SMC) via MultiVeStA for transient sensitivity analysis of the Keynes+Schumpeter (K+S) macroeconomic agent-based model.

nodes.title: A Multi-Method Validation Framework for Large-Scale Multilingual Text Analytics
nodes.summary: Presented at JADT 2026 and awarded the VADISTAT Prize for young researchers, this paper validates 18 analytical approaches on 1M+ texts to identify method-invariant findings.

nodes.title: Network Topology Analysis and Machine Learning Techniques for Systemic Risk Prediction in U.S. Equity Markets
nodes.summary: Leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and complex network theory to detect early warning signals of systemic risk in financial markets.

nodes.title: Robust Portfolio Optimization Under Systematic Market Disruptions: A Factor-Analytic Approach
nodes.summary: Based on my MSc thesis, this paper is currently in review at Computational Economics and develops a robust framework for portfolio optimization under contamination.
